question: How could all of Messed Up Dress Up's current features move to Hazel, piece by piece: what would two months of work bring over, what would three, and what has to be decided first?
inventory: 03 face, 04 hair, 05 ghost, 06 costumes, 07 underwear, 08 body
the face, hair, body, clothes, shoes, costumes, see-through layers: a picture from the settings
SVG text built by string functions; settings in one state object
17 moving and climbing (moveNow, the rig), part of 18 drawing
the pose rig, each animation's pose at a phase (walk, crawl, swim, climb, sit, lie, balance)
a phase from the music's clock (LFO B), the rig's joint maths
09 backgrounds, 10 nature, 11 houses and huts, 12 clearing and castle, 13 castle rooms and map, 14 outdoors, 15 place picker
about 40 places, castle rooms and tree rooms, each drawn from its settings; each thing standing there an object with a depth
SVG text; obj(name, depth, svg) for the depth sort; part() caches keyed on the settings read
the friend among the place's objects, by depth; the scene cache; still pictures on slow computers
Things in the way and walking
16 objects and solids, 26 drags and start (walks)
collision boxes and ovals, the back line, planned walks round them, the controller's steps
boxes MEASURED from the drawn picture (getBBox, getScreenCTM: 50 calls), then pure geometry
60 tunes as data (chords, parts, forms), the mixing board, LFOs the scenes follow
WebAudio for the sound; the tunes and the board are pure data
The world and its settings UI
every setting's control (1,337 rows in Background alone), the world designer, saves
26 drags and start (the rest), 22 full screen
pointer drags of joints and things, a game controller and the on-screen one, keys
DOM events, the Gamepad API, 60 polls a second
the picture archive (every place, the friend in it, as SVG plus its settings), the music archive, the speed gate
has: init, view and update, with splices (splice_new, splice_set, splice_eval): a livelit's model and its GUI, in the editor (integration branches, PR #2597 and #2635; not on dev)
slides already port pieces of the friend from this game: Polygons, Shirt and Pants, Shoes and Hair, Kids' Choice, the 1990s Face; each a picture built as SVG text from a model
SVG is text Hazel can build: floats with +. and friends, to_fixed for numbers, strings, lists of shapes drawn in order
records, labelled tuples, sums, System F over values (typfun, explicit @<T>); Modules II for libraries. No type application (no M(a) for a type constructor M)
a livelit release about 0.13 to 0.5 s on the faster branch (#2635) after this month's work (from 4.6 s), against under a millisecond for this game to draw the friend and 16 ms for a frame at 60 fps
lacks: walking, swimming, swaying scenery: a pose at a phase every frame

keep SMIL animations in the drawn SVG (they are text, and play without Hazel: the places' code writes animations in about 150 places today); per-frame motion stays in JS until a view can be fed time cheaply
60 frames a second leaves 16 ms; a Hazel evaluation of a view is 100 times that today
Hazel computes what a frame shows only when settings change; the JS loop moves the friend and plays the SMIL in between
collision boxes are measured from the DOM (getBBox) after drawing
compute each object's box from its geometry in the same function that draws it: a better design anyway, and testable
the tunes as Hazel data (they already are data), played by the JS synthesizer
a library module is copied into each slide
one program per piece, or a library mechanism first
A big program in the editor
22,000 lines of JS is perhaps 15,000 of Hazel
measure the editor's statics on a program that size early (the statics scaling probe of 10-09 found about 1.4 times the work on the slides, not re-analysis)
two: The settings as Hazel types: body, face, hair, clothes, background, as records with their defaults; a save's JSON read into them
every saved settings file in the picture archive parses and prints back the same
The friend's drawing: face, hair, body, clothes, shoes, as functions from settings to SVG text, ported part by part (03 to 08)
the archive's body, face, hair, shirt, pants, feet and costume pictures: same settings, same SVG, byte for byte
The pose rig and every animation's pose at a given phase (moveNow): pure maths
the archive's moves pictures, and poseJoints at sampled phases
The places, ten a week, the simplest first (the empty room, bubble space, the tent) to the castle's rooms; each thing an object with its depth
the archive's backgrounds pictures, place by place
The friend among a place's objects by depth: one picture of a frame, held still
the frame loop, input, collisions, walking, music, the controls, the world designer, saves
three: As the two-month plan, at a gentler pace where the castle rooms need it
Collision boxes computed from geometry, in the drawing functions, then the planner (planPath is pure already)
the archive's collision-box pictures; the planned-walk sweeps of tickets 332 and 358
The tunes and the mixing board as Hazel data; the scenes' LFO followers
the music archive's settings; the JS synthesizer plays the Hazel tunes and the MP3s match
The world designer as a livelit: the grid of places, their ways, each square's settings
a world saved in the game opens in the livelit and back
The settings' controls as livelit GUIs, Background first, the knolling of ^du_report(5) as their design
the frame loop, input, WebAudio, the archives' tools
risks: the friend's picture alone is a large view; if a release stays near half a second, a slider drag in Hazel feels slow next to the game's
measure the friend's drawing in Hazel in week 2, before porting further; ^report(1)'s series has the method
the places are 8,650 lines; ported straight they may strain the editor
a place per program, joined only by the settings types
the game keeps growing nightly (289 versions in a week); a port chases a moving target
freeze a version to port (0.0.289) and log what changes after it, or port only pieces the children have settled
nothing that runs per frame should go through Hazel's evaluator yet
Hazel decides what is drawn; JS moves it
decide: draws the same picture from the same settings (the oracle can check it), or runs the whole game in Hazel (needs a clock, input and sound Hazel lacks)
Playground slides, one piece each, or a library module and one program; slides cannot import each other yet
a frozen one, with the changes after it logged, or the moving game
the children, in the editor, or only the archive's oracle until the pieces join
next: the oracle (same settings, same SVG) or the whole game; this report assumes the oracle for two months
port the face alone (03 face, 431 lines) and time a release of its view in Hazel, before any schedule is believed
move collision boxes from DOM measuring into the drawing functions in the JS game first (it helps the game, and makes the port pure)
tag the version to port (dress-up-0.0.289) and keep a log of what changes after it
try the empty room, bubble space and the tent as three small programs sharing the settings types
Keep the JS as the engine
the frame loop, input and sound stay JS; Hazel supplies the pictures, as a livelit's view does

livelits: Cyrus Omar, David Moon, Andrew Blinn, Ian Voysey, Nick Collins, Ravi Chugh. Filling Typed Holes with Live GUIs. PLDI 2021.
hazelnut: Cyrus Omar, Ian Voysey, Michael Hilton, Jonathan Aldrich, Matthew A. Hammer. Hazelnut: A Bidirectionally Typed Structure Editor Calculus. POPL 2017.
